package_info.package_versions: Multiple MSI motherboard models (potentially all affected by leaked keys)
package_info.why_malicious: The leak of extremely sensitive cryptographic signing keys (Boot Guard keys) enables attackers to create malicious firmware or bootkits that appear legitimate, subverting operating system security from the lowest levels.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malicious bootkit signed with leaked MSI Boot Guard private key
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At boot-time, the code executes as a signed bootkit, subverting OS controls by running before the operating system loads, enabling persistent and stealthy compromise.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Bootkits signed with OEM keys are highly privileged and can bypass all OS-level security, making detection and remediation extremely difficult.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normally, only trusted OEMs can sign firmware/boot code. Here, attackers can sign arbitrary malicious code, violating the trust model of secure boot.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate firmware updates signed by the OEM for security or feature updates.
key_indicators: Use of leaked OEM signing keys
Bootkits that pass secure boot validation

attack_chain.action: Attacker obtains leaked MSI Boot Guard signing keys from dark web.
Attacker crafts malicious bootkit or firmware image and signs it with the leaked key.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious firmware appears legitimate to secure boot.

attack_chain.action: Malicious firmware is installed on target system (via physical access, supply chain, or remote exploit).
attack_chain.leads_to: Bootkit executes at boot, subverting OS security.

attack_chain.action: Bootkit persists and operates with highest privileges, enabling further attacks (e.g., credential theft, rootkit installation).
attack_chain.leads_to: Full system compromise, difficult to detect or remediate.

behavioral_signatures: Firmware/bootloader images signed with known-leaked OEM keys
Boot-time code execution that bypasses OS-level security controls
file_indicators: UEFI/BIOS images with signatures matching leaked MSI keys
Unusual or unauthorized firmware update files
network_indicators: N/A (attack is local/firmware-level, but may enable later C2 traffic from compromised OS)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for firmware/bootloader images signed with known-leaked MSI Boot Guard keys. Use hardware attestation and secure boot logs to detect unauthorized firmware changes. Alert on any firmware updates not issued by the OEM or not matching expected cryptographic signatures. Consider hardware-based root of trust and out-of-band firmware integrity checks.
